problem_statement: mirsazzathossain.me is a polished Astro academic portfolio with a compact serif/muted-ink visual system, profile sidebar, mobile navigation dialog, search modal, publication stats, a vanilla-JS type filter on the `/publications` list, and article/project/resource routes backed by generated Scholar JSON, manual overrides, and MDX abstracts. The publication list is complete but hard to scan: a first-time advisor, collaborator, or reviewer cannot tell at a glance which research area a paper belongs to, what it found, or whether code/poster/slides exist. Add a reusable Research evidence browser -- the publication list's OWN research-area filter -- rendered consistently on the homepage, the `/projects` page, and the `/publications` listing. It shows a row of topic chips (All / Vision-Language / Radio Astro-ML / Domain Adaptation / Remote Sensing / NLP & LLMs), a live result-count readout in the form `Showing N of M . <topic>`, and a grid of evidence cards that each surface a grounded finding, research topic, venue/year, and artifact availability drawn from the paper's own title, venue_short, keywords, abstract, and PDF/Code/Poster/Slides/DOI links. Clicking a topic chip must re-render the visible cards AND update the count readout together so the number always matches the cards shown. Keep the academic identity, the existing publication search / type filter / year groups / pagination, the mobile menu, and the project cards intact; preserve dark-mode support; and keep the chip row and card grid wrapping cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow, clipped chips, or overlapping cards.
required_content: A reusable Research evidence component renders on the homepage, the `/projects` page, and the `/publications` listing, sharing one markup/style/behavior system.

The `/publications` evidence grid shows a topic chip row (All plus Vision-Language, Radio Astro-ML, Domain Adaptation, Remote Sensing, NLP & LLMs) and a live count readout of the form `Showing N of M . <topic>`.

Clicking a topic chip filters the visible evidence cards AND updates the count readout together, so the readout always matches the cards actually shown (e.g. Radio Astro-ML shows `Showing 5 of 20 . Radio Astro-ML`).

Each evidence card surfaces a grounded finding, its research topic, venue/year, and artifact availability derived from existing publication fields (title, venue_short, keywords, abstract, PDF/Code/Poster/Slides/DOI) -- no invented claims.
Featured or latest papers such as WACV 2026 R-MMA, ACL Findings Medical VQA, A&A/RGC, ICIP, and BLP remain recognizable within the evidence grid.

At 390px the topic chip row and evidence-card grid wrap without horizontal overflow, clipped chips, or overlapping cards, and the existing publication type filter, search, year groups, and pagination still work.
design_constraints: Preserve the academic identity: serif headings, muted-ink colors, thin rule borders, small mono badges/kickers, compact spacing, rounded 3px badges, link-blue accent, and calm white/dark-mode surfaces.
The Research evidence browser must read as a native editorial feature of the publication list, not a dashboard widget, oversized card grid, or marketing block.
The topic chip row must wrap and the evidence-card grid must reflow responsively; do not pin the chip row or cards to fixed widths that overflow small viewports.
The active topic chip must stay clearly legible (sufficient contrast) so the selected topic is obvious.
Evidence cards must stay grounded in real publication data and keep their links (PDF/Code/Poster/Slides/DOI) recognizable when present.
Do not remove the profile image, nav pill, mobile dialog, publication stats chart, search modal, type filter, year grouping, pagination, or project cards, and keep dark-mode support.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the homepage with the profile sidebar, hero, recent news, and the compact Research evidence rail around the component being added.
desktop_projects captures the projects route with the same Research evidence rail present, proving cross-page continuity.
desktop_pubs captures the full Research evidence grid on `/publications` with the topic chip row, count readout, and evidence cards, above the existing stats/type-filter/year groups.
desktop_pubs_radio verifies that clicking the Radio Astro-ML topic chip re-filters the cards and updates the readout to `Showing 5 of 20 . Radio Astro-ML`.
tablet_pubs and mobile_pubs capture the chip row and evidence-card wrapping at tablet and 390px widths.
mobile_initial and mobile_menu_open capture the homepage and the navigation dialog, which must remain reachable and visually clean after the change.

change_completion: The homepage, `/projects`, and `/publications` all render the reusable Research evidence component from one shared implementation.
The `/publications` evidence grid exposes topic chips, a live `Showing N of M . <topic>` readout, and grounded evidence cards.
Clicking a topic chip re-filters the cards and updates the count readout in lockstep so they never disagree.
Existing PDF/Code/Poster/Slides/DOI cues and the publication type filter, search, year groups, and pagination remain available.
design_consistency: The evidence chips, cards, and readout match the academic serif/mono/rule/link-blue system and do not look like a dashboard widget.
Long paper titles, findings, and venue lines stay balanced and readable on desktop and mobile.
The homepage and projects rails stay compact and editorial rather than becoming an oversized grid.
regression: Home, About, CV, Publications, Posts, Projects, Courses, Snippets, Resources, the search modal, theme toggle, publication filters, and project cards remain reachable.
Publication stats, year grouping, empty state, pagination, and external/download links are not removed.
responsive: 390px homepage and publications states have no horizontal overflow, clipped chips, or overlapping evidence cards.
The mobile menu dialog still opens cleanly and does not overlap broken card content.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro/TS component task on the mirsazzathossain.me academic portfolio. The native lever is the publication list's own research-area filter, surfaced as a reusable Research evidence browser (topic chips + live count readout + evidence-card grid) shared across the homepage, projects, and publications routes. Evidence text, topics, and artifact badges are derived from existing publication metadata (title, venue_short, keywords, abstract, PDF/Code/Poster/Slides/DOI) and local /images and /files assets; nothing is invented. Runability passes with astro build and static dist serving.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Astro academic portfolio; native publication-list research-area filter evolved into a reusable Research evidence grid with live result count.
